findings.title: getClientsWithPermission only finds resources whose type is 'Clients'
findings.body: Per-client resources are created in `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` via `resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, owner)`, and no type is ever set on them. Only the 'Clients' all-resource has type 'Clients'. `findByType` therefore returns at most that all-resource, so the method returns {"Clients"} instead of client IDs. As a result, listing clients will not work through per-client permissions.

findings.title: Possible NPE when all-clients resource missing
findings.body: `getResourceTypeResource` can return null, for example when a realm's admin-permissions client was initialized before 'Clients' was added to the schema. The null is passed to `findByResource` and then dereferenced in `resource.getScopes()`, which throws an NPE. That would surface as a 500 on admin client endpoints.

findings.title: Removal listener gated on V1 feature only
findings.body: The listener is now gated on `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ`, which skips cleanup when only V2 is enabled. That avoids the UnsupportedOperationException from `ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled`. However, if V1 and V2 are both enabled, `management()` returns MgmtPermissionsV2, so deleting a client calls `setPermissionsEnabled` and throws. Separately, V2 per-client resources and permissions are never removed when their client is deleted, leaving orphaned resources.

findings.title: Per-client permission shadows all-clients permission
findings.body: If a per-client resource exists, only that resource is evaluated and the 'Clients' all-resource is never checked. For example, a per-client VIEW permission removes a MANAGE grant the admin has through an all-clients permission, because the fallback only runs when no specific resource exists. Note that the caller's `canManage` short-circuit does not cover this case.
